experiment: the certificate promoted from a quadruple to a split of the whole population, swept against a noise floor

floor_sweep.question: Is there a noise floor at which every clonal population reads as a tree while every reticulate one does not, and the reticulate ones still certify something? A floor so high that nothing is certified makes everything a tree and answers nothing, so an empty system does not count.

matched_null_floor.how_replicates_are_matched: Each null replicate is accepted only if its OWN realised divergence is within the tolerance of the population's. This is rejection sampling on the realised nuisance, not matching in expectation. It is necessary rather than fastidious: `tuning-bias` measured the relaxed-clock divergence at fixed mu to have a coefficient of variation near 50% and a 10x-28x spread between extremes, so a floor taken as a max over mean-matched replicates is dominated by whichever replicate drew a fast-rate tree.

preregistered.M1: every non-reticulate population reads as a tree under its own matched floor
preregistered.M2: every reticulate population reads as a non-tree
preregistered.M3: the reticulate ones still certify something, so an empty system cannot masquerade as a verdict
preregistered.M4: a planted recombinant appears in a witness quadruple

matched_null_floor.why: The constant-rate sweep failed, and the per-dataset breakdown said why: the saturated population keeps its certified splits at a floor 64x higher than the one that wipes out every other dataset, because saturation inflates margins IN RATE TERMS. A single global rate is the wrong functional form -- the same conclusion the null-floor surrogate reached when its fit put a large coefficient on divergence. So the floor is calibrated per population against a clonal null matched on taxon count, length, gap load, clock spread and divergence.

the_definition_and_why_it_is_a_conjuncti: Bandelt and Dress define a split's isolation index as a MINIMUM over the quadruples straddling it. Under complete deletion within the subset every quadruple has its own denominator, so that minimum would be an incommensurable comparison. The certificate is instead a logical CONJUNCTION of per-quadruple integer comparisons, each exact over its own denominator, needing no common metric.

P4_planted_taxon_in_a_witness_quadruple.note: The first version of this test also accepted the recombinant appearing anywhere in the incompatible pair's splits. A split's two sides cover every taxon, so that form is true whenever any incompatible pair exists -- a forced test. Only the witness quadruple, four taxa of nine, carries information, and that is what is counted here.

P5_every_witness_really_violates_four_po.claim: the constructed witness violates four-point on every dataset-seed-floor; a check on the theorem rather than a restatement of it

the_negative_control_failed_at_zero_floo.finding: With no floor, the lift is NOT a certificate of reticulation. A clonal strict-clock population with no reticulation certified more splits than its tree has and produced incompatible pairs.
the_negative_control_failed_at_zero_floo.mechanism: On an exact tree metric a quadruple's two crossing sums are EQUAL, so the middle split's isolation index is exactly zero. With finite data they differ by sampling noise of order sqrt(L), and `own < max(cross)` reads the sign of that noise. The first exhibit had sums [66, 110, 112] over a denominator of 2000: a 2-count margin.

the_theorem_being_exhibited: Two certified splits that are INCOMPATIBLE force a four-point violation, with a witness quadruple CONSTRUCTED from one taxon per side-intersection rather than searched for. Proved as `third_pairing_strictly_largest_of_two_certified` and `fourPoint_violated_of_two_certified`; the four-set instance (`fourSet_splits_pairwise_incompatible`) proves the claim earlier editions asserted, that no two splits of a four-set are compatible.
why: A quartet certificate names four sequences; what a biologist reads is a split -- this group against that group.
